title: Tarmac ops 1:1 prep and follow-up
content:
Purpose: quick personal prep for this week’s tarmac ops 1:1s + capture immediate follow-ups after each sync. Not the official runbook — my working notes and commitments.

Context: release train looming (week-of 2026-03-15). Focus areas: model switch A->A-quantized, routing fallback policy, smoke test coverage for embed/embeddings endpoint, final traffic shaping on Dedicated pools. Risk appetite: low for customer-facing regressions, medium for internal-only telemetry gaps.

Agenda (for 15m 1:1s):
- 00-02: quick health check (are you blocked)
- 02-06: 2 high-priority items I own (status + blockers)
- 06-10: 1 owner item I’m tracking for you (confirm owner + ETA)
- 10-13: go/no-go flags we need to raise today (explicit yes/no)
- 13-15: actions, owners, 24h commitments

Pre-meeting notes (what I need from them):
- SRE (Liam): confirm pressure test schedule + which Dedicated pool we will use for canary (pool-3). Also verify rollback job artifacts exist in GCS.
- Model infra (Priya): confirm quantization artifact hash + known perf delta at sequence=256. If >8% token latency increase, we shift to A-lite.
- Console (Marco): dashboard slices for rollout route, token-cost delta gauge, and top-5 traces for error 503s. Need these up-to-date before Thursday.

Go/No-go flags (quick checklist I’ll read off):
- Canary runs done (smoke pass >=95%): YES/NO
- Rollback image available & tested: YES/NO
- Dedicated pool capacity reserved: YES/NO
- Critical telemetry (latency, errors, qps) present on dashboard: YES/NO
- Key customer contracts notified (if >5% perf regression): YES/NO

My current risk register (personal shorthand):
- R1: model quantization at scale — unknown regressed tokens per second under long-context (seq=1024). Mitigation: run two 30-min long-context jobs overnight; if latency tail >200ms/pkt, switch to A-lite. Owner: Priya.
- R2: routing fallback mis-match — policy may send to wrong region under burst. Mitigation: temp disable cross-region routing for first 6 hours post-rollout. Owner: Marco + Networking.
- R3: billing spike due to cache-miss during rollout (regen warmup). Mitigation: pre-warm top-20 prefixes and enable conservative batching. Owner: myself (Ava).

Notes-to-self (phrases, reminders):
- "Ask for concrete ETA not vague 'today'"
- "If someone says 'works locally' ask for exact config and docker image id."
- "Write the rollback command on the card and confirm one engineer can run it end-to-end in <10m."

Follow-ups template (what I capture in meeting):
- Action: <short task> | Owner: <initials> | Due: YYYY-MM-DD | Done: yes/no | Blockers: <notes>

Immediate actions captured (post-1:1 today):
- Action: Schedule long-context perf jobs (2x 30m) on pool-stage-extended | Owner: Priya | Due: 2026-03-02 | Done: no | Blockers: need GPU time window
- Action: Add rollback image link to runbook + test smoke rollback in staging | Owner: Liam | Due: 2026-03-03 | Done: no | Blockers: access to customer-data staging key
- Action: Add a 'routing-fallback-enabled' toggle to console with 1-click disable | Owner: Marco | Due: 2026-03-04 | Done: no | Blockers: UI time; can do API-only if blocked
- Action: Pre-warm KV cache prefixes for top-20 prompt hashes from last week | Owner: Ava | Due: 2026-03-03 | Done: no | Blockers: script needs minor refactor (see gist link in slack thread)

Open questions I'm carrying into next syncs:
- Is pool-3 capacity committed for the full 48-hour post-rollout window, or only initial 6h? (Need clarity for rollback economics)
- If quantized model shows higher hallucination rate on structured-output tests, do we hold rollout or limit to non-customer-facing routes?
- What is minimum set of traces we need to keep for 30d retention vs cost? (Ops wants shorter retention but product wants 30d)

Quick decision heuristics (personal):
- Any customer-facing correctness regression (precision drop) -> BLOCK rollout until fixed.
- Latency tail increase up to 5% tolerated if cost savings >12% and no error increase.
- Any untestable rollback -> BLOCK.

Post-meeting capture checklist (do this immediately after each 1:1):
- Update actions table in this doc and ping owners in Slack with one-line summary + link to runbook.
- Snapshot dashboard time-range (last 2 hours) and attach link in Confluence ticket.
- Confirm rollback image ID in Slack thread and tag SRE on-call.

Where I stash quick evidence (personal links):
- perf job logs: gs://redwood-inference/tmp/perf-runs/2026-03-01/ava
- rollback images: gcr.io/redwood-inference/rollback-images/release-2026-03-15
- quick traces: traces.redwood.internal/short/RT-3421

Final note: keep this doc terse — copy final action items into the shared runbook only after I validate owners confirmed in Slack. This is my operational memory during the tarmac week.
